topic.title: Why does a 5,614 km fence cut Australia in two?
topic.map_answer: the fence's line itself: drawn across South Australia, New South Wales and Queensland, it puts the dingo country of the north and centre on one side and the sheep country of the south-east on the other

shape.name: The patrol
shape.beats: hook: the line across the continent and the question -> how long it is against something the viewer can feel -> a truck starts driving it from one end, the counter climbing -> what lives on each side, shown on the map -> why it was built, the sheep in the south-east -> the turn: it used to be even longer -> payoff: what it really holds back -> loop back to the line
shape.why: a why-shaped story whose answer is one line on the map, followed end to end by a patrol truck as its kilometres count up

title: What is Australia's 5,614 km fence keeping out?
description:
A single fence runs across Australia from the coast to the outback. What is it keeping out?
The Dingo Fence, followed end to end on the map: dingo country on one side, sheep country on the other.
